cards.stem: What relationship between lift and wing area is highlighted as a key scaling principle
cards.quote: Like the other aerodynamic force, drag, the lift is directly proportional to the area of the object.
cards.hint: Think about how area scaling affects aerodynamic force

cards.stem: What product defines the total aerodynamic force acting on a body moving through air
options: the pressure times the surface area
cards.quote: The total aerodynamic force is equal to the pressure times the surface area around the body.
cards.hint: Recall what combination creates force from pressure

cards.stem: How is the lift component oriented relative to the path of flight
cards.quote: Lift is the component of this force perpendicular to the flight direction.
cards.hint: Consider direction versus motion through air

cards.stem: What design action is taken to sustain lift during takeoff and landing at lower velocity
cards.quote: Takeoff and landing are times of relatively low velocity, so to keep the lift high (to avoid the ground!) designers try to increase the wing area.
cards.hint: Think about what must be enlarged to keep lift high
